category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title names the same-numbers-repeated trap (real Grade-1 misconception) but rationale never cites named research and recovery_moves do not branch by diagnostic ('if child can produce one alternative / if child cannot').
category_feedback.required_fix: Anchor the trap in named research (Falkner, Levi & Carpenter 1999; Carpenter, Franke & Levi 2003 — operational vs relational view of equality) and branch recovery_moves: (a) if child produces ONE alternative pair, scaffold near-doubles shift 5+5 to 4+6; (b) if child produces none, drop to counters and physically split 10; (c) if variety is addition-only, model 11-1 on the balance.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: differentiation.for_movement_learners says 'Use the balance scale physically' but no explicit no-paper / no-purchase alternative path. Lesson still requires per-pair counters (~30), drawing mats, target card deck, and printed tracker — not runnable on a no-prep day.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit no-materials alternative in differentiation: 'No-prep version — use children's fingers as counters (two hands = 10), draw the balance scale on the whiteboard with one marker, call targets verbally. Children whisper expressions to a partner instead of writing.' Makes Lesson 4 runnable in any classroom on any day per Level 4.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Bella and Bobby anchor minds_on and consolidation, vocabulary is child-friendly, and all success_criteria start with 'I can'. But there is no distinctive quotable Bella refrain or memorable chant — consolidation just lists discussion_prompts and a generic exit sticky-note format.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a Bella refrain children chant at consolidation, e.g., 'Same total, NEW way — that's equivalent!' — repeated by Bella every time a new pair is found, and built into the exit_routine ('Read your sticky aloud: Same total, NEW way!'). Gives the unit a memorable thread per Level 4 descriptor that children carry between lessons.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Lesson teaches equivalence conceptually with the balance scale and includes subtraction and 3-term sums (solid L3). But children are never invited to invent or COMPARE strategies, and expanded_walkthrough does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms (operational vs relational equality).
category_feedback.required_fix: In action step 4, have two pairs share lists side-by-side and name the moves they used (commutative swap, near-doubles shift, subtraction inverse). Cite the operational-vs-relational view of equality (Carpenter, Franke & Levi 2003) in expanded_walkthrough.rationale. Invite children to invent their OWN move ('What's a new way nobody has shown?').

summary: Lesson 4 is a solid C2.3 implementation: alignment and lesson-worksheet consistency hit Level 4, with a concrete same-numbers-repeated trap and a faithful 3-part worksheet. Four categories sit at Level 3 — trap lacks named research and branched recovery, no no-prep alternative, no quotable Bella refrain, no strategy-comparison move. Tighten these for a pass.
